mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months indicates the Federal Reserve is shifting from tightening to easing, lowering discount rates and boosting equity valuation multiples, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in easing regimes are not statistically higher than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns in tightening regimes are not significantly lower than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for three consecutive months indicates a strengthening labor market, prompting firms to expand capital spending and lift earnings expectations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in strengthening labor regimes are not statistically higher than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) below 150,000 for two consecutive months signals a weakening labor market, prompting firms to reduce capital expenditures and lower earnings forecasts, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns in weakening labor regimes are not significantly lower than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 for three consecutive months indicates softening demand for manufactured goods, compressing corporate earnings and equity valuations, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in softening demand regimes are not significantly lower than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above 110 for two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand environment, prompting firms to ramp capital spending and lift earnings expectations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns in strengthening demand regimes are not statistically higher than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 237 for three consecutive months indicates a disinflationary environment, reducing policy rate uncertainty and boosting risk appetite, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns in disinflation regimes are not significantly higher than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 240 for two consecutive months signals accelerating price pressures, prompting tighter monetary policy and higher discount rates, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns in accelerating inflation regimes are not significantly lower than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
